correctness.rationale: The n distinct ordinal outcomes are exactly the n circular Kronecker gaps. The regular q_k-point grid approximation yields all-gap maximum 3/q_k through its denominator interval and defect at most log(3(a_{k+1}+1)). For a_{k+1}=a≥16 and b=floor(a/log a), the b q_k observations form disjoint q_k-point-centered clusters; their q_k(b-1) intracluster gaps each have size |q_k α-p_k| and total mass ε<1/log a. Shannon conditioning yields defect at least log b-h(1/log a)-log(b-1)/log a, hence log a-log log a-1-o(1); together both sides give the sharp block ratio 1 and the bounded-type equivalence. The packaged checker passed 77 finite ordinal-pattern tests and 703 numerical bounds, but none of the infinite theorem is inferred from these tests.

originality.rationale: The full prior all-slope normalized-entropy theorem detects the irrationality exponent only; the new bounded-additive-defect iff bounded partial quotients and M_k/log a_{k+1}->1 for large quotients are not implied. Goda supplies the geometrical separation theorem but no entropy converse or sharp block law; proving the latter requires disjoint convergent clusters and the conditional Shannon bound. Relevant full texts and matching published statements were compared; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A pre-existing equivalent theorem may be indexed under entropy of Sturmian word frequencies or Kronecker partition information, without mentioning ordinal patterns.
The full historical literature on gap entropy has not been exhaustively searched; novelty is best-knowledge, not independently certified.

value.rationale: Finite-order ordinal uncertainty is widely used despite vanishing entropy rates for rotations. The bounded-additive-error property has a natural KL-divergence interpretation and an exact arithmetic classification across all irrational slopes. The sharp log a block size distinguishes exponent-two frequencies that the leading all-slope normalized information spectrum provably identifies together; this is neither a routine fixed numerical example nor a restatement of zero entropy.
